create.name: Olympia Zen Center
create.bio:
Olympia Zen Center, also known by its temple name Ryoko-an, has offered Soto Zen practice in Olympia, Washington, since 1995. Its founder and abbot, Eido Frances Carney Roshi, began sitting with Kobun Chino Otogawa in the early 1970s, trained as a priest at Shoboji in Iwate Prefecture, where she was the first woman and the first foreigner to do so, and in 1997 was given Dharma transmission by her teacher Niho Tetsumei Roshi. A former president of the Soto Zen Buddhist Association, she stands in the lineage of the hermit poet Ryokan and founded the Order of Ryokan to bring his poetry and life to modern readers.

The community is mainly lay, with residential practice also available. Zazen and morning ceremony run from Tuesday to Friday; Wednesday evenings open with an orientation for newcomers, then sitting, ceremony and a Dharma talk; and Saturday mornings combine zazen, temple cleaning, breakfast and the study of classic Soto texts. A one-day retreat is held each month, with longer sesshin in summer and at Rohatsu in December, and most sessions can be joined on Zoom. Teaching is given freely, supported by donations, with scholarships for retreats.

courses.title: Rohatsu Sesshin
courses.description: The year's most intensive retreat, marking the Buddha's awakening: from an evening opening on 1 December to breakfast on 6 December, with days of zazen from 5:30 am to 9 pm, private interviews with the practice leader and a closing ceremony. Join for all or part, in person or on Zoom.
courses.price: $150 for the entire sesshin, or $35 per day donation requested, plus dana for the practice leader

courses.title: One-day Retreat
courses.description: The monthly day-long retreat, held on a Saturday from morning to late afternoon: zazen, walking meditation, ceremony, a formal Soto-style lunch and temple work practice, with private conversation with the practice leader after lunch.
courses.price: $35 to $50 donation, plus dana for the practice leader

courses.title: Wednesday Evening Practice and Newcomer Orientation
courses.description: A weekly evening that begins with an introduction to Zen practice for newcomers, followed by zazen, a short ceremony, a Dharma talk and social time. No experience or registration is needed.

courses.title: Saturday Practice
courses.description: Saturday mornings of zazen and ceremony, temple cleaning, a shared breakfast and a discussion of texts from the Soto tradition, open to newcomers and also available on Zoom.

free_resources.title: Olympia Zen Center Study Texts and Liturgy
free_resources.description: Downloadable PDFs for home practice and study: the centre's chanting and ceremony guide, the Song of Ryokan, a Shobogenzo text and instructions for formal oryoki meals.
